To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the DNA-incorporated radionuclide iodine-125, which is a potent emitter of Auger electrons, induces more double-strand breaks in nuclear DNA of mammalian cells than do other radiations, and that these breaks are caused by indirect effects.
the DNA damage caused by decay of the DNA-incorporated Auger-electron emitting radionuclide iodine-125 is not only direct but also indirect.
the decay of DNA-bound 125I induces DSBs and that these DSBs can be prevented by DMSO.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the biological effects produced by DNA-incorporated Auger electron emitters and with the mechanisms involved in the formation of DNA damage
elucidating the mechanism of DSB formation in mammalian cells exposed to the decay of DNA-bound 125I and with understanding the role of indirect mechanisms in DSB formation.
the mechanism of DNA damage induced by decay of DNA incorporated 125I.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, for the same level of DSBs, DMSO provides greater protection against gamma rays than against 125I decay.
the decay of DNA-125I induces more DSBs in mammalian cells than would be expected if only the direct effects of the Auger electrons were considered.
DMSO protects nuclear DNA from both gamma-ray and 125I decay-induced DSBs, and the protection is more effective against DSBs induced by gamma rays.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
DMSO protects DNA from DSB induction caused by the decay in the presence of DNA of the Auger-emitting radionumcide 125I.
, for the same level of DNA strand breaks (DSBs), DMSO can more efficiently protect DNA from gamma-ray-induced DSDs than from DSBs induced by the decay of 125I in DNA.
the DNA-incorporated Auger-electron emitter 125I induces a higher yield of DSBs per decay than does the gamma emitter 137Cs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the decay of 125I in DNA induces DSBs through both direct and indirect mechanisms.
DSBs produced by 125I decay are not simply the result of direct effects on the DNA.
the decay of 125I in nuclear DNA induces DSBs by both direct and indirect mechanisms.
